title: Audit telemetry: encryption, schema evolution, and contract guarantees for SIEM/webhook sinks
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: As customers adopt Dedicated and Private deployments and enable tenant-scoped audit sinks (Splunk/Datadog/Generic webhooks), we must guarantee secure delivery, forward-compatible schemas, and strong privacy controls. Previous tickets solved delivery/backpressure and dedup semantics, but we need an end-to-end proposal that binds: envelope-level encryption (CMK support), event signing, a schema-versioned envelope contract, PII redaction rules, and explicit admin controls exposed via RBAC v2 to manage sink configurations.

Goal: Define and implement an audit-envelope contract and enforcement for all external sinks that ensures confidentiality in transit and at rest, deterministic schema evolution with graceful decoder fallback, verifiable delivery guarantees (idempotency + DLQ patterns), and admin-level controls (who can create/modify sinks, rotate keys, and toggle raw vs. redacted payloads). This will be an audit-pipeline-level change with backward-compatible protocol headers for existing integrations.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every external audit sink accepts events wrapped in the new envelope format (Content-Type: application/vnd.redwood.audit-enveloped+json; version header) or is covered by a compatibility passthrough flag.
- Envelope supports: schema_version, tenant_id, event_id (UUID v4), timestamp, hmac_signature, enc: {alg,kid,iv,ciphertext}, metadata for routing.
- KMS-backed envelope encryption using customer-managed keys (CMK) is supported for Private/Dedicated customers; hosted default uses Redwood-managed keys.
- HMAC signing key rotation and verification endpoint in Console documented.
- Delivery guarantee SLO: 99.95% of events delivered to configured sinks within 30s under normal load; at-least-once with idempotent dedup semantics implemented via event_id and per-sink dedupe window.
- DLQ per-sink with per-tenant isolation and observable metrics (DLQ size, oldest message age).
- Admin RBAC v2 scopes: sink.create, sink.update, sink.delete, sink.read, sink.rotate_keys, sink.toggle_raw.
- Integration docs and example client for Splunk/Datadog/Generic webhook updated and published.
- Security review completed and threat model updated in Confluence.

decisions:
- Use an enveloped JSON format rather than changing existing event bodies to minimize downstream changes.
- Backwards compatibility: sinks can opt-in to 'compatibility mode' where the platform will also deliver raw event bodies for a 60-day migration window.
- Encryption: AES-GCM envelope encryption with a KMS-wrapped data key; support for customer-managed keys (CMK) in Private/Dedicated.
- Signing: HMAC-SHA256 over the canonicalized envelope headers and ciphertext to detect tampering and replay.
- Idempotency: event_id + per-sink dedupe index; at-least-once semantics with client-side or adapter dedup recommended for exactly-once where possible.
- Redaction: two modes - raw (no redaction, requires admin scope sink.toggle_raw) and redacted (PII fields removed by redact service before envelope).
- Rate-limiting/backpressure: token-bucket per-sink with observable headroom; when saturated, delay delivery with exponential backoff and surface metrics and alerts; persistent failures move events to DLQ after N retries (configurable per-sink).

notes:
- Edge cases: downstream SIEM connectors that perform schema-based routing may need a lightweight shim that validates and extracts event.payload after decrypting; provide a sample shim in Go and Python.
- Migration path: 1) announce envelope; 2) open compatibility window where both raw and enveloped events are delivered; 3) provide an opt-in strict mode per-sink; 4) deprecate compatibility after 60 days or negotiated enterprise timeline.
- Performance: envelope + GCM adds ~1.5ms per-message CPU on current runtime nodes; quantify at 10k eps in load test.
- Observability: add metrics for envelope_decrypt_latency, envelope_hmac_mismatch_count, per-sink_retry_count.
- Privacy: redact service rules are maintained in a policy file per-tenant; require Workspace Admin scope to modify.
- Admin controls: tie sink roles to SSO groups via SAML attribute mapping; Console will show last-rotation timestamp and who rotated keys.
- Failover: if CMK unreachable, fallback to Redwood-managed key if tenant allows; otherwise pause sink and emit administrator alert.
- Implementation order recommendation: design -> shim + docs -> KMS + signing -> adapters -> Console RBAC UI -> deprecation window.
